title: Dal Tadka
subtitle: Indian spiced red lentils with a tempered butter finish
excerpt: Dal tadka is two things in one pot: the cooked lentil base and the sizzling tadka of spices and onion that goes on top. The tadka is made in a separate pan and poured over at the very last moment -- this is not an optional garnish but the part that makes the dish. Use sunflower oil instead of ghee to keep this fully vegan.
sourceNotes: Dal tadka is a staple of North Indian dhaba cooking, roadside restaurants serving truck drivers and travellers. The tadka -- a bloom of whole spices in hot fat poured over the cooked dal just before serving -- is the defining step that gives the dish its aromatic punch.

recipe.freezeNotes: Dal freezes very well for up to 3 months. Reheat with a splash of water and the tadka freshly made on top.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch. The tadka should always be made fresh and added just before serving.

content.text: Red lentils do not need soaking and cook fast. Watch the heat -- once they are soft they catch on the bottom quickly. Keep the heat low and stir regularly in the last 10 minutes. Ghee gives the tadka richness; swap for sunflower oil to keep this fully vegan and dairy-free.

items.prepNote: or sunflower oil to keep vegan

content.text: Put the rinsed lentils in the saucepan with 1 litre of cold water. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, and reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring regularly, until the lentils are completely soft and falling apart. Add more water if needed to keep a loose, soupy consistency. Stir in the turmeric halfway through.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp of ghee (or sunflower oil) in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft and starting to colour. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the ground cumin, ground coriander, and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute.

Add the fresh tomatoes and tinned tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Stir the tomato mixture into the cooked lentils. Add the garam masala and season well. Simmer together for 5 minutes.

For the tadka, heat the remaining 2 tbsp of ghee in a small frying pan over high heat until very hot. Add the cumin seeds and mustard seeds and cook for 20-30 seconds until they are popping and fragrant.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal immediately. Add the lemon juice, stir once, and scatter with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or flatbread.

items.cause: Too much water evaporated during cooking.
items.fix: Stir in 100-200 ml of hot water and cook for a further 2 minutes.

items.cause: Pan too hot or spices left unattended.
items.fix: Work fast once the spices go in -- they only need 20-30 seconds. Pour immediately over the dal the moment they start to pop.
